title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: THE LOST RING
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Terrence Mabry, a hotel repairman in Myrtle Beach, South Carolina.
Terrence can fix anything. Ice machines. Elevators.
But one summer, the ocean broke something he couldn't fix.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE WAVE
segments.quote: Nothing contributes so much to tranquilize the mind as a steady purpose.
segments.author: Mary Shelley
lines: On their twentieth anniversary, his wife Nicole jumped a wave, laughing.
When she came up, her wedding ring was gone. Somewhere in a mile of sand.
Terrence couldn't sleep. Then he remembered Mary Shelley, who wrote Frankenstein:
Nothing contributes so much to tranquilize the mind as a steady purpose.
Next day, he bought a ninety-dollar metal detector at a pawn shop.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE TEETH
segments.quote: Life is far too important a thing ever to talk seriously about.
segments.author: Oscar Wilde
lines: Week one, he dug up bottle caps, a spoon, and somebody's false teeth.
His coworkers howled.
Then his buddy Luis quoted Oscar Wilde:
Life is far too important a thing ever to talk seriously about.
So Terrence laughed too, and hung the teeth in the break room. They still smile at everybody.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: MISS ETTA
segments.quote: Patience and time do more than strength or passion.
segments.author: Jean de La Fontaine
lines: Every dawn he swung that detector like a tennis racket. Nothing.
Then he met Miss Etta, a seventy-eight-year-old retired shrimp boat cook.
She quoted the French storyteller La Fontaine:
Patience and time do more than strength or passion.
So he slowed down. Low, slow sweeps, at low tide.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE WRONG RING
segments.quote: The greatest pleasure I know is to do a good action by stealth, and to have it found out by accident.
segments.author: Charles Lamb
lines: In August, the beep was gold. A man's wedding band, engraved Harold and June.
Miss Etta quoted the English writer Charles Lamb:
The greatest pleasure I know is to do a good action by stealth, and to have it found out by accident.
Terrence found Harold in Conway, and left the ring in his mailbox, no name.
Harold's doorbell camera caught him anyway. Harold sent a pecan pie.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: SECOND WAVE
segments.quote: Character consists of what you do on the third and fourth tries.
segments.author: James Michener
lines: By October, a wave knocked him flat and shorted out the detector.
Terrence said, That's it. I quit.
Nicole read him a line from James Michener:
Character consists of what you do on the third and fourth tries.
He dried the detector with her hair dryer and went back out the next morning.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: FOUND
segments.quote: Whatever our souls are made of, his and mine are the same.
segments.author: Emily Brontë
lines: Now Nicole came along every Saturday with two coffees and a beach chair.
One morning after a storm, the detector sang. Ten inches down. Her ring.
Nicole held it, then quoted Emily Brontë, from Wuthering Heights:
Whatever our souls are made of, his and mine are the same.
Terrence got down on one knee in the sand, and asked her again.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Find a purpose. Laugh. Go slow. Do good quietly. Try again. Love deeply.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Find a purpose. Laugh at the false teeth. Go slow. Do good quietly. Try a fourth time. Love deeply.
I tried a metal detector once. Found my own car keys. Very proud.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
